hook.line: Vale calls from Medellín and Tomás can hardly speak. The kindest thing she can say is not advice. It is to tell him his reaction makes sense.
hook.es: No me extraña que estés tan cansado.
hook.en: No wonder you're so tired. (to a man)

examples.es: No me extraña que estés tan disgustado.
examples.en: No wonder you're so upset. (to a man)

examples.es: Me imagino lo que debes de estar pasando.
examples.en: I can imagine what you must be going through.

examples.es: No me extraña nada que se haya ido.
examples.en: It doesn't surprise me at all that she left.

examples.es: No me extraña que Vale esté cansada.
No me extraña que no durmieras anoche.
examples.en: No wonder you didn't sleep last night. (to a friend)
I can imagine what you feel. (to a friend)

rule:
To tell someone their reaction makes sense, Spanish has two warm options.
*No me extraña que* + subjunctive: "no wonder...". Add *nada* to press the point: *No me extraña nada que...*
*Me imagino lo que* + verb: "I can imagine what...".
English says "no wonder you're upset" with a plain verb. Spanish puts the verb in the subjunctive (*estés*, *esté*, *durmieras*), because it is a reaction to the fact.
Try these instead of *te compadezco*, which can sound distant.
smallPrint: Teachers call *no me extraña que* an expression of emotion, which takes the subjunctive.

readAndPick.es: No me extraña que estés tan disgustado.
options: It surprises me that you're so upset.
No wonder you're so upset.
I'm sorry you're so upset.

readAndPick.es: Me extraña que estés tan tranquilo.
options: No wonder you're so calm.
I'm glad you're so calm.
It surprises me that you're so calm.

readAndPick.es: No me extraña nada que se haya ido.
options: It doesn't surprise me at all that she left.
It surprises me that she left.
I'm not surprised she'll leave.
I imagine what I feel.
I imagined what you felt.
I can imagine what you feel.

readAndPick.es: No me extraña que no durmieras anoche.
options: No wonder you didn't sleep last night.
No wonder you won't sleep tonight.
I didn't sleep last night.

readAndPick.es: No me extraña que Vale esté cansada.
options: Vale is surprised that I'm tired.

options: I can't imagine what you're going through.

I'm not surprised that I want to sell.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *estés* or *estás*, then type the whole sentence: No me extraña que ___ tan disgustado. (No wonder you're so upset. To a man.)
yourTurn.answer: No me extraña que estés tan disgustado.
yourTurn.why: After *no me extraña que*, the verb is in the subjunctive: *estés*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *esté* or *está*, then type the whole sentence: No me extraña que Vale ___ cansada. (No wonder Vale is tired.)
yourTurn.answer: No me extraña que Vale esté cansada.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: No wonder you didn't sleep last night. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: No me extraña que no durmieras anoche.
yourTurn.why: It happened last night, so the verb takes the *-ra* form: *durmieras*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I can imagine what you feel. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Me imagino lo que* is followed by an ordinary verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: It doesn't surprise me at all that she left.
yourTurn.answer: No me extraña nada que se haya ido.
yourTurn.why: *Nada* presses the point, and *haya ido* is the subjunctive for a past event.

yourTurn.prompt: Press the point with *nada*: *No me extraña que estés tan disgustado.* becomes: It doesn't surprise me at all that you're so upset. (to a man)
yourTurn.answer: No me extraña nada que estés tan disgustado.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about Vale, a woman: *No me extraña que estés tan cansado.* becomes: No wonder Vale is so tired.
yourTurn.answer: No me extraña que Vale esté tan cansada.
yourTurn.why: For *Vale* the subjunctive is *esté*, and a woman is *cansada*.

pitfalls.wrong: No me extraña que estás tan disgustado.
pitfalls.right: No me extraña que estés tan disgustado.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *no me extraña que* the verb is in the subjunctive: *estés*.

pitfalls.right: No me extraña que estés cansado.

pitfalls.wrong: Te compadezco por lo que pasas.
pitfalls.right: Me imagino lo que debes de estar pasando.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Te compadezco* can sound distant; *me imagino lo que...* sounds like a friend.

personal: Think of a friend who had a rough week. Tell them their reaction makes sense with *No me extraña que...*
